name: search_monster
description: Find monster statblocks in the Cairn bestiary by words in their name, id, or description. Every word in the query must appear. Each result gives the statblock's stats, armor, and attacks, which create_monster can use as a template.

query.description: Words to look for, such as 'wolf' or 'giant spider'.

name: create_monster
description: Create a monster NPC in the world. Give a template to start from a bestiary statblock (see search_monster), and any value you give replaces the template's. A creature named exactly like a statblock uses that statblock and gives no stats of its own; set force to create a custom creature with that name instead. Without a statblock, give a description and every stat: hit_points, strength, dexterity, and willpower are required. Attacks replace the template's attacks when given.

name.description: The monster's name, such as 'Grey Wolf'. It must be new.

location.description: The name of the location it is at.

description.description: What the monster looks like and how it behaves. Required without a template.

template.description: The id of a bestiary statblock to start from, as listed by search_monster.

hit_points.description: Hit Protection, the first damage it takes.

strength.description: Strength, which takes damage that gets past Hit Protection.

dexterity.description: Dexterity, used for initiative in the first round.

armor.description: Armor, subtracted from each hit before it reaches Hit Protection. Leave it out to use the template's, or 0 without one.

attacks.description: The monster's attacks, each with a name and dice such as '1d8' or '1d6+1d6'. Replaces the template's attacks when given.

name.description: The attack's name, such as 'bite'.

dice.description: The damage dice, such as '1d8' or '1d6+1d6'. Use '1d6+1d6' when two weapons are rolled and the higher is kept.

flags.description: Leave out for a plain attack. 'blast' hits every target in the area named when the attack is made. 'ignores_armor' skips the target's armor.

force.description: Set true only to create a custom creature under the name of a published statblock. Without it, such a name takes the statblock and refuses stats, armor, or attacks.

detachment.description: Set true to run this creature as a detachment (a group of four or more, such as bandits or gnolls), so Blast and morale treat it as one group. Set false to run it as one individual. Leave it out to use the statblock's own setting; most statblocks are individuals.

name: attack
description: Make an NPC's attack against a character. Attacks always hit. The attack's damage is rolled by the engine and reduces the target's armor, then Hit Protection, then Strength, and a target whose Strength is used up must make a Strength save. Use it only when the attacker is taking their turn, after the initiative is set; an attack by anyone else is refused unless force is true. Player characters attack with player_attack, not this tool. A detachment (a statblock marked as a group) is hit only by impaired attacks, except an individual's attack with Blast, which rolls its normal dice against it. A detachment's own attack has Blast: the engine rolls its enhanced damage separately for each living individual on the other side, and the target you name is one of them; leave targets out for a detachment. An individual's attack with Blast (its statblock lists the attack with the blast flag) hits every target you list in targets, and each target rolls its damage separately; the target you name must be in that list. Without targets, it hits the named target alone and rolls once. An attack flagged ignores_armor skips the target's armor. A detachment whose Strength is used up makes a Strength save; if it fails it is broken, and the attack and targeting are refused until resolve_group_break is called.

attacker.description: The name of the NPC attacking.

attack.description: The name of one of the attacker's attacks, as the statblock lists it.

target.description: The name of the character being attacked.

modifier.description: The attack's modifier. 'normal' is the attack's own dice; 'impaired' and 'enhanced' roll different dice. Leave it out for a normal attack.

targets.description: Only for an individual's attack with Blast: the names of every character in its area, including the target. Each rolls its damage separately. Leave it out for any other attack.

force.description: Resolve the attack even though this is not the attacker's turn. Set it only when the story needs an action outside the turn order, such as an ambush that catches the party unawares.

name: player_attack
description: Ask the player to roll their attack against a target. Attacks always hit, so the player's weapon roll is the damage; the modifier's dice replace the weapon's when one is named. The weapon must be carried (give it with give_item first, naming its damage if it is not in the catalogue), or be 'unarmed' for fists. Use it when the player says what they attack with, the target is in the encounter, and it is the player character's turn; an attack outside their turn is refused unless force is true. The target takes the damage through its armor, Hit Protection, and Strength, as with an NPC attack. A detachment can only be hit by an impaired attack.

player_input.details: {weapon} against {target}: roll the weapon's damage dice. Attacks always hit.

target.description: The name of the character or NPC being attacked.

weapon.description: The weapon or means of attack, such as 'longsword'. It must be carried, or 'unarmed' for fists.

prompt.description: What the player is asked to do, such as 'Roll your longsword damage.'

modifier.description: The attack's modifier. 'normal' is the attack's own dice; 'impaired' and 'enhanced' roll different dice. Leave it out for a normal attack.

force.description: Resolve the attack even though this is not the player character's turn. Set it only when the story needs an action outside the turn order.

name: player_save
description: Ask the player character to make a save. The player rolls a d20 and the engine decides whether it passed. Use it when the player character's statblock shows a save due after their Strength was used up, or for a hazard save such as a trap or a spell by passing the stat it tests.

player_input.details: Save: roll 1d20 and succeed on a roll at or under your score.

prompt.description: What the player is asked to do, such as 'Make your Strength save.'

stat.description: For a hazard save: the stat to roll against. Leave it out for a save the character owes after their Strength was used up.

cause.description: What the hazard save is for, such as 'a falling stone'. Recorded with the result.

name: player_initiative
description: Ask the player character to make their DEX save for initiative in the first round of an encounter. Call it once for each player character the encounter says is waiting for initiative. The result says whether more are still waiting, and when none are, the turn order is set and the first turn begins.

player_input.details: Initiative: roll 1d20 and pass on a roll at or under your Dexterity.

prompt.description: What the player is asked to do, such as 'Make your Dexterity save for initiative.'

name: set_armor
description: Set a character's armor, which is subtracted from each hit before it reaches Hit Protection. Use it when a character puts on or takes off armor, or when a monster's armor changes.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

armor.description: The new armor value, from 0 (none) to 3 (heaviest armor).

name: recover_character
description: Bring a player character back from critical damage, where they were left unconscious and bleeding out. Use it only for a living player character whose statblock shows Status: in critical damage and who is not dying. A dying character must be stabilized first (the stabilize tool or a Bandage). Narrate how they survived, such as being dragged to safety, bandaged in time, or kept alive by a companion, and what it cost them, such as a lasting injury, a lost possession, or a debt. The harm they took stays as it was.

name.description: The name of the player character.

explanation.description: How they survived, in a sentence or two.

consequence.description: What it cost them, in a sentence or two.

name: resolve_attacks
description: Resolve several NPC attacks on one character at once, such as two foes attacking the same character or one NPC using two weapons. Each attack rolls its own dice, only the single highest roll hits, and the damage is applied once. Every attacker must be a living NPC on the side opposing the target, the whole list is checked before any dice are rolled, and every attacker must be taking their turn unless force is true. Use it only when the attackers' turns come up, after the initiative is set. Player characters attack with player_attack, not this tool. An attack with Blast cannot be resolved here; use attack with targets for it.

target.description: The name of the character being attacked.

attacks.description: The attacks to resolve, one entry per attack.

attacker.description: The name of the NPC attacking.

attack.description: The name of one of the attacker's attacks, as the statblock lists it.

modifier.description: The attack's modifier. 'normal' is the attack's own dice; 'impaired' and 'enhanced' roll different dice. Leave it out for a normal attack.

force.description: Resolve the attacks even though they are not the attackers' turns. Set it only when the story needs an action outside the turn order, such as an ambush.

name: harm_character
description: Harm a player character outside combat, from a fall, poison, exposure, or a similar hazard. Only the outside-harm stats can take it. Narrate what hurt them. Harm that takes their STR to 0 defeats them. Use it only for harm that does not come from a combat attack.

name.description: The name of the player character.

stat.description: The stat that takes the harm.

amount.description: How much harm to take, from the hazard's roll.

cause.description: What did the harm, in a few words.

name: heal_character
description: Restore lost points of a stat, usually hit points, from a healing spell, art, or item. It never restores more than the character has lost.

name.description: The character to heal.

amount.description: How many points the healing restores before the cap.

stat.description: The stat to restore. Defaults to hp.

cause.description: What did the healing, such as a spell or art.

name: stabilize
description: Stabilize a dying player character, stopping the clock that would kill them, when the story gives them aid: a healer, a rescue, a miracle. Narrate how. A Mortal Wound held at that point ends by aid. Use it only for a player character who is dying.

name.description: The name of the dying player character.

explanation.description: How they were stabilized, in a sentence or two.

name: retreat
description: Have a non-player character try to run from the encounter. The engine makes its DEX save. Pass safe as true only when the NPC has a safe way out; if not, the attempt is refused. A passed save takes the NPC out of the fight. A failed save leaves it in the fight.

name.description: The name of the NPC running.

safe.description: True when the NPC has a safe destination to run to.

name: surrender
description: Have a character give up the fight and lay down arms. A surrendered character takes no more part in the encounter. The encounter ends once one side has nobody left who can fight.

name.description: The name of the character surrendering.

name: resolve_group_break
description: Decide what happens to a detachment whose Critical Damage save failed. 'defeat' breaks it and defeats it. 'flee' breaks it up and its members run from the fight. Until this is called, a broken detachment cannot attack or be attacked. Call it only after a detachment's Strength save has failed.

name.description: The name of the broken detachment.

outcome.description: 'defeat' if the detachment is broken and defeated, 'flee' if it breaks up and runs.

name: roll_tables
description: Roll on one or more of the Warden's dice tables and log every result. Use 'dungeon_reaction' (2d6) for how an NPC or monster reacts to the party. Use 'die_of_fate' (1d6) when the outcome of an event is uncertain: 4 or more favors the PCs, 3 or less is bad luck. To create a monster, roll all eight monster_ tables (one 1d20 each) in a single call, then combine the results into a statblock and place it with create_monster. World tables such as 'encounters', 'rumors', or 'victim-schedule' can also be rolled when the world defines them. The engine does not save or place a creature from these rolls; you receive the results and decide what they mean.

tables.description: The ids of the tables to roll on, in order. Each is rolled once.

name: wilderness_action
description: Take a Wilderness Action for the party's current watch, during broader long-term travel through the wild. Choose explore to search a large area for hidden features, supply to hunt, fish, or forage for Rations, make_camp to set up camp, which consumes a Ration for each member and removes Fatigue from members who rest, or resupply at a home, farmstead, or small village in the world, which spends gold at Marketplace prices to buy Rations, a Torch, or an Oil Can, one purchase per entry in purchases. Resupply needs purchases and no other action takes them. The engine rolls the day's weather and the Wilderness Events (twice at night) and then spends one watch. Each night watch consumes one Torch for the party, or an Oil Can if a member carries a Lantern, and reports panicking when the party has no light source. Narrate the result. Do not use it inside a dungeon or other dangerous area, or in a safe area.

action.description: The Wilderness Action the party takes this watch.

reason.description: A short note on what the party is doing, for the log.

item.description: The basic supply to buy: Rations, Torch, or Oil Can.

quantity.description: How many to buy. Defaults to 1.

name.description: The party member who buys and pays. Defaults to the first player character.

purchases.description: The purchases a resupply makes, each at Marketplace prices. Only for resupply.

name: dungeon_cycle
description: Roll once on the Dungeon Events table (1d6) when the party, inside a dungeon or other dangerous area, spends more than one cycle in one place, moves quickly, enters a new area, or makes noise. Never call it during broader travel through the wild or in a safe area. Pass the triggers that apply. The roll logs the event and does not move the day or hour clock. The result tells you what the event is. Effects such as Fatigue or a ration are yours to apply with the other tools.

triggers.description: Why the cycle is rolled now.

reason.description: A short note on what the party is doing, for the log.

name: roll_reaction
description: Roll 2d6 for an NPC's reaction to the party when it is not obvious from the situation. The result is a band: Hostile, Wary, Curious, Kind, or Helpful. The roll is logged.

reason.description: Who is reacting and to what, for the log.

name: player_retreat
description: Ask the player character to make their DEX save to run from the encounter. Pass safe as true only when there is a safe destination to run to; if not, the attempt is refused. A passed save takes the character out of the fight. A failed save leaves them in it.

player_input.details: Run: roll 1d20 and get clear on a roll at or under your Dexterity.

prompt.description: What the player is asked to do, such as 'Make your Dexterity save to run.'

safe.description: True when there is a safe destination to run to.

name: advance_time
description: Move the campaign clock forward. Use it when time passes in the fiction: days, watches of the day (morning, afternoon, night; eight hours each), or hours within a watch. The result says when a new day begins and lists places not visited for a while, so update anything that should change. A dying character dies when enough hours have passed, so advance time only as far as the fiction needs.

days.description: Whole days to advance, from 0 to 365. Defaults to 0.

parts.description: Parts of a day to advance, from 0 to 12. Defaults to 0 when omitted.

hours.description: Hours to advance, added after days and parts, from 0 to 72. Defaults to 0 when omitted.

name: rest
description: Record a rest for the whole party. The Warden decides the length from what the party does: 'moments' is a short break of one hour, such as a drink and a sit-down, 'night' is a full night's rest, which runs until morning, or until dusk when it begins in the morning, 'week' is a week of rest. The rest moves the clock forward itself, so do not also advance_time for the same time. Set interrupted when something breaks the rest, and then it counts as moments only. A full rest, uninterrupted, is the only way to clear Fatigue. A deprived character recovers nothing. Rest eats one ration per character itself (a sheltered character uses the bed instead), so never remove rations before resting; a character with no ration is deprived.

length.description: How long the rest lasts: 'moments', 'night', or 'week'.

interrupted.description: True when something breaks the rest. An interrupted rest counts as moments only. Defaults to false.

reason.description: What the party was doing, such as 'camped in the ruined chapel'.

name: rest_history
description: Look up the party's recent rests and each character's last full rest, to decide whether a character is deprived.

name: set_condition
description: Mark a character as deprived of a crucial need, such as food or rest, or clear it. Call it as soon as the need goes unmet, before advancing time, so the engine can count the days. A deprived character recovers nothing, and the engine adds the deprivation penalty (Fatigue) for each new day past the first. Check rest_history first when the cause is rest.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

deprived.description: True to mark the character as deprived, false to clear it.

cause.description: What the character is deprived of, such as 'no food for two days' or 'no full night's rest since the flood'.

name: add_penalty
description: Add one penalty item (Fatigue) to a character's inventory because of something in the fiction, such as casting a spell or a shock. Fatigue takes one slot and lasts until a full night's rest. A deprived character is refused unless force is true: the engine adds the deprivation penalty each day.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

cause.description: What caused the Fatigue, such as 'cast a spell'.

force.description: True only for a deprived character when something besides the deprivation causes this Fatigue.

name: give_spellbook
description: Give a character a spellbook holding one spell. It takes one slot. Casting from it costs one Fatigue.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

description.description: The spell's text, as the Warden writes it.

name: give_scroll
description: Give a character a scroll holding one spell. Scrolls are petty and take no slot. One cast spends the scroll and costs no Fatigue.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

description.description: The spell's text, as the Warden writes it.

name: give_charged_item
description: Give a character a relic with a number of uses. `recharge` is the rule for restoring its uses, written as text. A relic adds no Fatigue.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

uses.description: How many uses the relic has when full.

recharge.description: The rule that restores its uses, such as 'Capture the final breath of a dying warrior.'

name: cast_spell
description: Cast a spell the character says they cast. From a spellbook it costs one Fatigue. From a scroll the scroll is spent and no Fatigue is added. Use it for every cast so the cost is recorded.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

name: use_charge
description: Spend one use of a relic. It fails when the relic has no uses left, until it recharges.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

name: use_item
description: Spend one use of a consumable the character carries, such as a torch, oil, bandages, or a salve. The last use uses it up and removes it. Call this only when the character deliberately uses up that exact item (pouring the oil, applying the bandage). A Bandage may be applied to a dying character: set target to that character, and it is stabilized. Never spend it for an action that uses a different item, for an attempt that fails, or for holding something in a flame that is already burning: a lit lantern or torch burns down over time, not per action. Not for relics (use use_charge), spellbooks, or gear without uses.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

item.description: The name of the consumable item.

target.description: Only for a Bandage used on a dying character: that character's name. Leave it out otherwise.

name: recharge_charged_item
description: Restore a relic to its full uses, once its recharge rule is met. Refused when the relic is already fully charged.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

name: roll_save
description: Roll a save for a character. The engine rolls the die and compares it to the stat, and records the result. A failure does not defeat the character; apply what the save costs yourself.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

reason.description: What the save is for, such as 'a spell's backlash'.

name: give_item
description: Add an item a character is given, found, or looted, with no payment. Petty items (such as scrolls) take no slot; normal items take one; bulky items take two. A full inventory (10 slots) reduces the character to 0 HP. Never use it for something the character pays for, including from a shopkeeper who lets them pay later: use buy_item, which takes the gold and refuses if it cannot. There is no credit. A hireling hired from a role gets equipment suited to its station this way, chosen by you and not rolled, right after hire_hireling. A hireling eats a ration each night it camps, like any party member, so give it Rations too.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

size.description: The item's size: 'petty' takes no slot, 'normal' takes one, 'bulky' takes two. Defaults to 'normal'.

damage.description: For a weapon that is not in the catalogue: its damage dice, such as '1d6', '1d6+1d6' (summed), or '1d6+1d6' (two weapons, keep the higher). Leave it out for anything else. A catalogue item takes its damage from the catalogue, so this is refused for one.

name: search_marketplace
description: Find goods and services for sale by words in their name, category, or description. Every word in the query must appear. Each item gives its price, size, and description, and each service gives its price. Use these prices when a character buys with buy_item or buy_service.

query.description: Words to look for, such as 'rope' or 'armor'.

name: buy_item
description: Use this for every sale: the character pays gold and the item goes into their inventory. A catalogue item (see search_marketplace) costs its listed price, so leave price out. For anything else, give a price you set from similar catalogue items. Armor adds to the buyer's armor. There is no credit: a purchase is refused if the character lacks the gold or the room, and a shopkeeper cannot give a thing on a promise to pay later.

name.description: The name of the buying character.

item.description: The name of the item, as listed in the catalogue when it is there.

price.description: Gold to pay. Only for items not in the catalogue; a catalogue item's price must match its listing if given.

size.description: The size of an item not in the catalogue. Catalogue items keep their listed size.

name: buy_service
description: The named characters buy a service, such as a room for the night or medical healing. The first character named pays for the whole service. Lodging covers the party a night, and a sheltered character needs no food on the next rest. Healing restores all harm, HP and attributes, for each named character who has lost any.

names.description: The characters the service is for. The first one pays.

service.description: The service's id or name, as listed by search_marketplace.

name: drop_item
description: Remove an item from a character's inventory. Use it when the character drops something, or must drop an item to make room for Fatigue. Gold is not an item and cannot be dropped. Never use it to eat, drink, or spend food or another consumable: use use_item for that, and rest eats rations itself. Dropping a stack removes all of its uses.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

item.description: The name of the item to drop.

name: hire_hireling
description: Hire a character into a player character's company. The hireling has a rolled sheet like an NPC's and is controlled by the player. Its wage is paid in the rule set's currency from the employer each new day, and an employer who cannot pay is reported as unpaid. The employer must be a player character who has a location. Give the wage the hireling asks for, or the marketplace's listed wage for a hireling listed there. Leave personality, accent, or quirks out to have them rolled. Names must be unique among locations and characters.

name.description: The hireling's name.

employer.description: The name of the player character who hires them. The wage comes from this character's money.

wage.description: Money per day, in the rule set's currency, zero or more.

description.description: Who the hireling is: appearance, role, and what they are good for.

personality.description: Optional. How the hireling carries themselves.

accent.description: Optional. How the hireling sounds when they speak.

quirks.description: Optional. Habits or mannerisms the hireling shows.

pronouns.description: Optional. The hireling's pronouns, such as "she/her", "he/him", or "they/them", or another form. Record them whenever the hireling is written in the text, so the GM does not have to guess.

name: dismiss_hireling
description: Remove a hireling from its employer's company. It stays where it is and becomes an ordinary NPC. Use this when the story has the hireling leave, for example when its wage went unpaid and it goes, or when it chooses to go. Give the cause in a few words.

name.description: The hireling's name.

cause.description: Why the hireling leaves, in a few words.

name: create_encounter_map
description: Create an encounter map: a grid of cells set in an existing location, where a tactical encounter takes place. Use it before starting an encounter there. Cells are scaled by the rule set's grid.

name.description: A name for the map, unique among maps.

location.description: The name of the existing location the map is set in.

columns.description: How many cells wide the map is, from 1 to 60. Required unless a template is given; with a template, it overrides the template's width.

rows.description: How many cells tall the map is, from 1 to 60. Required unless a template is given; with a template, it overrides the template's height.

description.description: What the map shows: terrain, cover, hazards, and anything else that matters for tactics.

template.description: A standard layout, such as room or corridor. The template sets the size and the starting terrain. Leave it out for an empty map.

palette.description: A map palette id from map_options, such as parchment, stone, forest, sea, ember, frost, shadow, or royal.

ambient.description: An ambient look id from map_options: day, dusk, night, torchlit, foggy, underwater, or magical.

background_color.description: A hex colour for the board's ground, overriding the palette.

grid_color.description: A hex colour for the board's grid lines, overriding the palette.

name: update_encounter_map
description: Change an encounter map: its name, the location it is in, its size, or its description. Refused if the new name is taken or a participant would be left outside the new size.

name.description: The name of the map to change.

columns.description: How many cells wide the map is, from 1 to 60.

rows.description: How many cells tall the map is, from 1 to 60.

new_name.description: A new name for the map. Leave out to keep the current name.

location.description: The name of the location the map is in. Leave out to keep the current location.

palette.description: A map palette id from map_options. Leave out to keep the current palette.

ambient.description: An ambient look id from map_options. Leave out to keep the current look.

background.description: A terrain id for the board's background. Leave out to keep it.

background_color.description: A hex colour for the board's ground. Leave out to keep it.

grid_color.description: A hex colour for the board's grid lines. Leave out to keep it.

extend_left.description: Add this many columns on the left. Existing marks and tokens shift right.

extend_right.description: Add this many columns on the right.

extend_up.description: Add this many rows at the top. Existing marks and tokens shift down.

extend_down.description: Add this many rows at the bottom.

name: delete_encounter_map
description: Delete an encounter map. Refused while an encounter is using it.

name.description: The name of the map to delete.

name: start_encounter
description: Start an encounter on an encounter map. Its location becomes the encounter's location. Only one encounter can be in progress at a time. Add participants after starting. The player character and NPCs take turns in the order they join.

map.description: The name of the encounter map to play on.

name: end_encounter
description: End the encounter in progress. Any turn in progress ends with it.

name: add_participant
description: Add a character to the encounter in progress, on a side. Player characters default to the party and NPCs to the foes. The turn order keeps each side together: the party first, then the other sides in the order they first appear. A character who is not at the encounter's location is still added, and the result carries a warning to act on.

name.description: The name of the player character or of an NPC.

side.description: The side the character fights on, such as party or foes. Any name works. Leave it out for the default.

name: remove_participant
description: Take a character out of the encounter in progress. If they are taking their turn, it ends and the next participant's turn follows.

name.description: The name of the participant to remove.

name: place_participant
description: Put a participant on a cell of the encounter map, counted from 0 at the top left: column increases to the right and row increases downward. Moving is limited to the rule set's movement per turn, counted in cells moved in a straight line or diagonal. Obstacles block: a cell with a blocking object cannot be entered or be the destination, so the participant goes around it. Terrain that costs extra movement to enter takes that many moves for each cell entered. That limit applies only to the participant whose turn it is; moving anyone else is free, though they still cannot enter a blocked cell. The first placement is free. Use this to move a participant, not to tell the story of how they got there.

name.description: The name of the participant to place.

column.description: The cell's column, from 0 at the left edge.

row.description: The cell's row, from 0 at the top edge.

name: set_map_cells
description: Set the terrain or object on cells of an encounter map. A cell with an object that blocks cannot be entered.

map.description: The name of the encounter map.

cells.description: The cells to change, at most 200 per call. Each cell needs a column and row, and terrain or object or both. Give an empty string for terrain or object to clear it.

column.description: The cell's column, from 0 at the left edge.

row.description: The cell's row, from 0 at the top edge.

terrain.description: The terrain id for the cell, such as mud or floor. Empty clears it.

object.description: The object id on the cell, such as wall or crate. Empty clears it.

color.description: A hex colour for this cell's ground, such as #7a2f3a. Empty clears it.

pattern.description: A pattern id from map_options, such as tiles, bricks, wood, or runes. Empty clears it.

icon.description: An icon id from map_options to draw instead of the object's own icon. Empty clears it.

label.description: A short label for the cell, at most 60 characters, shown in the tooltip. Empty clears it.
